title: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
summary: Covers financial fraud, fake job offers, investment scams, and deception where someone induces a victim to deliver money or property.
full_text: Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
cognizable: Cognizable (Police can arrest without warrant and register FIR)
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine
remedy_steps: Gather digital evidence immediately: bank transaction statements, UPI transaction IDs, WhatsApp/email communications, and scammer phone numbers.

If money was lost online, immediately call the National Cyber Crime Helpline at 1930 or lodge an online complaint at cybercrime.gov.in within the first 2-4 golden hours to freeze beneficiary accounts.
File a formal Police Complaint / FIR under Section 173 of BNSS (2023) at your local police station or Cyber Crime Police Station.
If police refuse to register FIR, submit a written complaint to the Superintendent of Police (SP) or file a private complaint before the Judicial Magistrate.

title: Criminal Breach of Trust
summary: Committed when someone is entrusted with property or money, but misappropriates, converts it to their own use, or dishonestly refuses to return it.
full_text: Whoever, being in any manner entrusted with property, or with any dominion over property, dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use that property, or dishonestly uses or disposes of that property in violation of any direction of law prescribing the mode in which such trust is to be discharged, commits criminal breach of trust. Punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine, or both
remedy_steps: Send a formal legal notice demanding return of entrusted assets/funds within 15 days.
Preserve proof of entrustment (receipts, agreements, emails, witness statements).
Lodge an FIR under Section 173 BNSS with the local police station.
Approach the Magistrate under Section 175(3) BNSS if police inaction occurs.

title: Theft and Punishment for Theft
summary: Taking movable property dishonestly out of someone's possession without their consent.
full_text: Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person's consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft. Whoever commits theft shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. In case of second or subsequent conviction, imprisonment shall extend to five years.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both (Up to 5 years for repeat offenders)
remedy_steps: Report theft immediately to police to obtain an FIR copy (needed for insurance and tracking).
Provide IMEI numbers (for mobile phones), vehicle registration details, or serial numbers.
Track lost phones via Central Equipment Identity Register (CEIR portal: ceir.gov.in).

title: Defamation and Community Service Provision
summary: Making or publishing false imputations intended to harm the reputation of any person. BNS 2023 introduces community service as a progressive penalty.
full_text: Whoever, by words either spoken or intended to be read, or by signs or by visible representations, makes or publishes any imputation concerning any person intending to harm the reputation of such person, is said to defame that person. Punished with simple imprisonment up to two years, or with fine, or with both, or with community service.
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to 2 years, fine, or community service
remedy_steps: Preserve verifiable records of defamatory statements (screenshots, URLs, print publications, audio).
Issue a Cease and Desist / Legal Demand Notice seeking unconditional apology and retraction.
File a private criminal complaint under Section 223 of BNSS before the Chief Judicial Magistrate.
Optionally file a civil suit for damages/compensation in Civil Court.

title: Criminal Intimidation
summary: Threatening someone with injury to their person, reputation, or property to cause alarm or force them to act against their will.
full_text: Whoever threatens another with any injury to his person, reputation or property, or to the person or reputation of anyone in whom that person is interested, with intent to cause alarm to that person, commits criminal intimidation. Punished with imprisonment up to two years or fine. If threat is to cause death or grievous hurt, imprisonment up to seven years.
bailable: Bailable (Simple) / Non-Bailable (Death/grievous hurt threat in certain states)
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or up to 7 years if threat of death/grievous hurt
remedy_steps: Record threatening phone calls, voicemails, or preserve threatening text messages.
File a Non-Cognizable Report (NCR) or FIR at police station depending on the severity of threat.
Seek police protection or an injunction order if imminent bodily harm is feared.

title: Stalking (Physical and Cyber Stalking)
summary: Following a woman, contacting or attempting to contact repeatedly despite clear disinterest, or monitoring her internet, email, or electronic communication.
full_text: Any man who follows a woman and contacts, or attempts to contact such woman repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest; or monitors the use by a woman of the internet, email or any other form of electronic communication, commits the offence of stalking. First conviction punishable with imprisonment up to 3 years and fine; second conviction with up to 5 years and fine.
punishment: Up to 3 years imprisonment (1st offence), up to 5 years (repeat)
remedy_steps: Do not delete stalking messages, emails, GPS trackers, or social media handles; keep chronological evidence.
Lodge complaint with Women Helpline (1091) or Cyber Crime portal.
File an FIR under Section 78 BNS at any local police station or All-Women Police Station.
Apply for protection orders under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act if stalker is known/family.

legacy_code: Section 154 of Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
title: Information in cognizable cases (Registration of FIR & Zero FIR)
summary: Mandates police to record First Information Reports for cognizable offences. Explicitly codifies Zero-FIR (filing at any police station regardless of jurisdiction) and electronic FIR (e-FIR).
full_text: Every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence, if given orally to an officer in charge of a police station, shall be reduced to writing by him or under his direction, and be read over to the informant. Information may be given electronically (e-FIR) or irrespective of the area where the offence was committed (Zero FIR). A free copy of the FIR must be provided immediately to the informant.
punishment: Departmental action and prosecution under Section 199 BNS against police officers refusing to register FIR
remedy_steps: You have the right to file an FIR at ANY police station in India (Zero FIR). The police cannot turn you away citing lack of jurisdiction.
Insist on receiving a free signed copy of the FIR immediately with the Crime Diary Number.
If the Station House Officer (SHO) refuses registration, send the complaint substance by registered post or email to the Superintendent of Police (SP) under Section 173(4) BNSS.
If no action is taken within statutory time, approach the Judicial Magistrate under Section 175(3) BNSS for orders directing investigation.

legacy_code: Section 50 & 50A of Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
title: Rights of Arrested Persons (Grounds of Arrest & Legal Aid)
summary: Every police officer arresting any person without warrant must immediately communicate full particulars of the offence, grounds of arrest, right to bail, and right to consult an advocate.
full_text: Every person arrested without warrant shall forthwith be informed by the police officer of the full particulars of the offence for which he is arrested or other grounds for such arrest. Where arrest is for a bailable offence, police must inform the person of their right to be released on bail. The arrested person has the right to meet an advocate of his choice during interrogation, though not throughout.
punishment: Illegal detention renders arresting officer liable for contempt and prosecution
remedy_steps: Ask the arresting officer politely: 'Under what section and grounds am I being detained?'
Ensure an Arrest Memo is prepared stating date, time, location, signed by at least one family member or witness.
Inform a nominated friend or family member immediately (mandatory under Section 48 BNSS).
Demand to meet an advocate or request free legal aid from Legal Aid Defense Counsel (NALSA).

legacy_code: Section 57 of Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
title: Person arrested not to be detained more than twenty-four hours
summary: No police officer shall detain in custody a person arrested without a warrant for a longer period than under all the circumstances of the case is reasonable, and such period shall not exceed 24 hours excluding journey time.
full_text: No police officer shall detain in custody a person arrested without warrant for a longer period than under all the circumstances of the case is reasonable, and such period shall not, in the absence of a special order of a Magistrate under Section 187, exceed twenty-four hours exclusive of the time necessary for the journey from the place of arrest to the Magistrate's Court.
punishment: Violation constitutes illegal confinement punishable under BNS Section 127
remedy_steps: Check the exact timestamp of detention on the arrest memo.
If 24 hours lapse without production before a Magistrate, family/counsel should immediately file a Habeas Corpus petition before High Court (Art. 226) or Supreme Court (Art. 32).
Advocate can move an urgent bail application before the Remand Magistrate.

title: Protection of Life and Personal Liberty
summary: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. Encompasses right to privacy, speedy trial, dignity, and livelihood.
full_text: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.
punishment: State compensation for illegal custodial torture or deprivation of liberty
remedy_steps: File a Writ Petition under Article 226 before the jurisdictional High Court.
For severe national or fundamental rights violation, move Article 32 before Supreme Court of India.
Petition State Human Rights Commission (SHRC) or National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) for custodial abuses.

title: Protection against arrest and detention in certain cases
summary: Guarantees that an arrested person cannot be denied right to be informed of grounds, right to consult legal counsel, and must be produced before magistrate within 24 hours.
full_text: (1) No person who is arrested shall be detained in custody without being informed, as soon as may be, of the grounds for such arrest nor shall he be denied the right to consult, and to be defended by, a legal practitioner of his choice. (2) Every person who is arrested and detained in custody shall be produced before the nearest magistrate within a period of twenty-four hours of such arrest.
punishment: Detention beyond 24 hours without magistrate order is unconstitutional
remedy_steps: Invoke Article 22 during police inquiry; inform police you wish to speak to an attorney.
If legal aid is unaffiliated, invoke Article 39A demanding free legal counsel.
Family members can demand immediate production before the Judicial Magistrate.

legacy_code: Directive Principle of State Policy & NALSA Act 1987
title: Equal Justice and Free Legal Aid
summary: State must ensure opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen by reason of economic or other disabilities, providing free legal aid.
full_text: The State shall secure that the operation of the legal system promotes justice, on a basis of equal opportunity, and shall, in particular, provide free legal aid, by suitable legislation or schemes or in any other way, to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen by reason of economic or other disabilities.
remedy_steps: Any person whose annual income is below statutory limit (or women, children, undertrials, SC/ST) is entitled to a free government lawyer.
Contact National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) toll-free helpline at 15100.
Visit the Legal Services Clinic situated in any District Court or Taluk Court complex.

title: Filing of Consumer Complaints & Redressal Forums
summary: Enables consumers to file complaints against manufacturers, traders, or service providers for defective goods, deficient service, or unfair trade practices.
full_text: A complaint, in relation to any goods sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or any service provided or agreed to be provided, may be filed with a District Commission by the consumer, or any recognized consumer association, or Central Authority. Pecuniary jurisdiction: District Commission up to ₹50 Lakhs; State Commission ₹50 Lakhs to ₹2 Crores; National Commission exceeding ₹2 Crores.
punishment: Refund, replacement, compensation for damages/mental agony, and punitive costs
remedy_steps: Send a written grievance or formal email notice to customer care/grievance officer of the company.
Call National Consumer Helpline (NCH) at 1915 or register complaint on consumerhelpline.gov.in.
File an e-daakhil petition on edaakhil.nic.in without physical court visits, paying nominal statutory fees.

title: Request for Obtaining Information and Timelines
summary: Empowers Indian citizens to request official records and answers from Public Authorities with strict 30-day compliance timelines.
full_text: A person who desires to obtain any information under this Act shall make a request in writing or through electronic means in English or Hindi or in the official language of the area, accompanying prescribed fee (₹10), to the Central/State Public Information Officer. The PIO must provide information within 30 days of receipt, or within 48 hours if it concerns the life or liberty of a person.
punishment: Penalty of ₹250 per day up to ₹25,000 on PIO for unjustified delay or refusal
remedy_steps: Identify the relevant Public Authority (e.g., Municipal Corporation, Ministry, University).
Draft concise, specific questions asking for existing records, orders, or files (avoid questions asking 'why').
File online at rtionline.gov.in (for Central ministries) or state RTI portals with ₹10 application fee.
If no reply is received within 30 days, file a First Appeal under Section 19(1) within 30 days to the First Appellate Authority (FAA).

title: Punishment for Cheating by Personation by using Computer Resource
summary: Penalizes individuals who cheat by impersonating someone else or creating fake digital profiles/accounts using any computer resource.
full_text: Whoever, by means of any communication device or computer resource, cheats by personation, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to one lakh rupees.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to ₹1,00,000
remedy_steps: Take screenshots of impersonating profile, message headers, and URL links.
Report profile on host platform (Instagram/Facebook/X/LinkedIn) for impersonation.
Lodge complaint on cybercrime.gov.in under 'Report Cyber Crime'.
Also invoke Section 319 BNS (Cheating by personation) in police FIR.

act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Application to Magistrate & Protection Orders
summary: Enables an aggrieved woman living in a shared household to seek immediate protection orders, residence orders, and monetary relief against domestic violence.
full_text: An aggrieved person or a Protection Officer or any other person on behalf of the aggrieved person may present an application to the Magistrate seeking one or more reliefs under this Act, including protection orders prohibiting acts of domestic violence, residence orders preventing eviction, monetary relief, and custody orders.
cognizable: Non-compliance with protection order is Cognizable & Non-Bailable (Section 31)
punishment: Breach of protection order punishable with imprisonment up to 1 year or ₹20,000 fine
remedy_steps: Contact the local Protection Officer (appointed in every district) or Service Provider NGO.
Dial Women Helpline at 181 or 1091 for immediate rescue or emergency shelter.
File an application under Section 12 before Judicial Magistrate First Class.
Court can grant ex-parte interim protection orders within 3 days of application.
